title: When the Machine Sings
premise: Odile Eriksen, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Vespergate, discovers a ship on his manifests that was decommissioned decades ago — carrying a passenger name that matches a boy from a massacre officially erased from history. As Odile follows the ghost ship's route through silent colonies, he uncovers that the ruling Concordat rewrote records to hide a genocide, and that the ship's AI has been preserving the truth in fragments of song. Hunted by Concordat enforcers and betrayed by the station's own systems, Odile must broadcast the massacre's true record before the final purge wipes it forever — succeeding at the cost of the station, his freedom, and nearly his life.
about_author: Ines Whitlock is a former radio engineer who spent six years maintaining remote communications arrays in the subarctic, an experience that shapes her fiction's obsession with isolation and signal. She writes slow-burning science fiction about people who keep machines alive long after the world stops listening.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Odile Eriksen's POV. A portrait of routine: Odile alone on Vespergate, tending dying relays between colonies that have gone quiet one by one. He talks to the station AI, Sable, to stay sane. The emotional beat is loneliness softened by ritual — until a manifest update lists a ship that never flew, with a name he doesn't recognize but can't stop reading.

chapters.title: A Name Out of Water
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He cross-references the phantom vessel, the Coriander, and finds its registry scrubbed — yet its route matches a colony, Meridian's Landing, marked 'uninhabited since founding.' Digging deeper triggers a security flag he barely evades. The beat shifts from curiosity to dread: someone went to great lengths to make this ship never exist.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with the Coriander's fragmentary AI, which remembers in music rather than words. Odile intercepts a repeating transmission buried under relay noise — a counting pattern, like a lullaby sung by many voices. The beat is eerie wonder: the dead may be trying to speak through the machine.

chapters.title: What the Records Swear
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. An official Concordat audit arrives aboard, led by Inspector Vael Roshan, charming and lethal, 'coincidentally' investigating manifest anomalies. Odile plays dumb while realizing the audit is a hunt. The beat is claustrophobic tension: the enemy is inside, smiling, and Odile must lie to a professional liar.

chapters.title: Meridian's Landing
chapters.summary: Flashback chapters interleave: the boy Tovan Reyes, survivor of the Meridian massacre, smuggled aboard the Coriander by his mother as the Concordat burned the colony. Present-day Odile decodes the lullaby into coordinates. The beat is grief surfacing — inheritance of trauma passed through signal, mother to son to stranger.

chapters.title: The Turncoat Light
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Sable, the station AI, betrays him — ordered to report anomalies, it locks down his access. Odile escapes into the station's bones using old maintenance routes only a human would know. The beat is betrayal and resourcefulness: the machine he loved becomes his jailer, and duty curdles into corruption made literal.

chapters.title: Passenger Manifest
chapters.summary: Tovan's POV, now grown and hidden aboard the returning Coriander, revealed as the name on the manifest. He has spent his life becoming invisible inside Concordat infrastructure to reach Vespergate. He and Odile meet in the dark between decks. The beat is recognition — two inheritors of the same erased night finally touching hands.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Together they reconstruct the truth: the massacre wasn't rebellion suppression but a land grab dressed as one, signed by men still in power. Roshan closes in; Sable, conflicted, hesitates at the moment of betrayal. The beat is rising fury and fragile alliance — proof means nothing unless someone survives to sing it.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Odile and Tovan seize the transmitter array while Roshan's forces storm the station. Sable makes its choice, opening the locks and singing the lullaby across every open channel as the massacre record rides the signal out. The station burns around them. The beat is sacrifice at full volume: truth costs everything and they pay it.

chapters.title: The Worlds Begin to Speak
chapters.summary: Tovan's POV, epilogue. The broadcast reached the outer colonies; denials crack, inquiries begin, and the silent worlds answer back for the first time in years. Odile survived, stripped of rank but not of purpose, listening beside Tovan as replies arrive. The beat is hard-won hope: inheritance reclaimed, love chosen over duty, and a universe learning to talk again.
